blocks.tk: Garagum çölüniň ortasynda, Aşgabatdan 260 kilometr töweregi demirgazykda, ýanyp duran uly çukur bar. Ol Derweze obasynyň golaýynda, şonuň üçin oňa Derweze gaz çukury diýýärler. Derweze sözi pars dilinden gelýär we “gapy” diýmegi aňladýar. Çukuryň resmi ady “Garagum ýalkymy”: ol bu ady 2018-nji ýylda alypdyr. Onuň diametri 60–70 metr, çuňlugy bolsa çeşmelere görä 20–30 metr. Çukuryň düýbünde we gyralarynda ýüzlerçe kiçi ot ýanýar: ýerden tebigy gaz çykýar we ýanýar.
blocks.en: In the middle of the Karakum desert, some 260 km north of Ashgabat, a large crater is burning. It lies near the village of Derweze, Darvaza in its Russian spelling, a name that comes from the Persian word for “gate”; in English the crater is often called the Door to Hell or the Gates of Hell. Its official name, given in 2018, is Garagum ýalkymy, the Shining of Karakum. It is about 60 to 70 m across and, depending on the source, 20 to 30 m deep. Hundreds of small fires burn on its floor and rim, fed by natural gas, mostly methane, seeping out of the ground.

blocks.tk: Bu çukur barada gürrüň köp, ýöne anyk maglumat az. Sowet döwrüniň resminamalary arhiwlerde ýok ýa-da olary görmek mümkin däl. Şonuň üçin çukuryň haçan we nähili dörändigini hiç kim anyk bilmeýär.
blocks.en: There are many stories about the crater but few firm facts. The Soviet records of how it began are missing from the archives, classified or out of reach, so nobody can say for certain when or how it formed.

blocks.tk: Iň meşhur gürrüň şeýle. 1971-nji ýylda sowet geologlary bu ýerde gaz gözläpdirler. Birden ýer çöküpdir we olaryň buraw enjamy ýerasty boşluga gaçypdyr. Ýerden zäherli gaz çykyp başlapdyr. Geologlar gazy ýakypdyrlar: olar gazyň birnäçe hepdäniň içinde ýanyp gutarjakdygyna ynanypdyrlar. Ýöne ot şondan bäri öçmändir. Bu gürrüňi köp habar gullugy we syýahat kitaby gaýtalaýar, ýöne ony tassyklaýan sowet resminamasy ýok.
blocks.en: The best-known account goes like this. In 1971 Soviet geologists were drilling here when the ground suddenly gave way and their rig fell into an underground cavity. Poisonous gas began to escape, so they set it alight, believing it would burn off within a few weeks. It has burned ever since. News agencies and travel guides repeat this version, and Live Science calls it the most widely circulated; but no published Soviet document confirms it, which is why Discover Wildlife presents it as “the story”.

blocks.tk: Başga gürrüňler hem bar. Kanadaly gözlegçi Jorj Kurunis ýerli geologlar bilen gürleşipdir. Olaryň aýtmagyna görä, çukur 1960-njy ýyllarda döräpdir, ony bolsa diňe 1980-nji ýyllarda ýakypdyrlar. Kurunis bu gürrüňi barlap bilmändir. Käbir çeşmelerde hatda 1950-nji ýyllar hem bar. Käbirleri geologlaryň gaz gözländigini, beýlekileri nebit gözländigini aýdýar.
blocks.en: Other versions exist. The Canadian explorer George Kourounis was told by local geologists that the crater collapsed in the 1960s and was only set alight in the 1980s; he said he could not verify this. A National Geographic photo caption even places the collapse in the 1950s. Accounts also differ on whether the drillers were looking for gas or for oil.

blocks.tk: Käbir zatlary bolsa anyk bilýäris. 2013-nji ýylyň noýabrynda Kurunis ýörite eşik geýip, çukuryň düýbüne düşüpdir. Ol çukuryň düýbüne düşen ilkinji adam. Kurunis çukuryň düýbünden toprak alyp gaýdypdyr. Alymlar bu toprakda yssa çydamly bakteriýalary tapypdyrlar. Bu bakteriýalar çukuryň daşyndaky toprakda ýokdy.
blocks.en: Some things are documented. In November 2013, on an expedition backed by National Geographic, Kourounis put on a heat-reflective suit and breathing gear and became the first person known to reach the bottom of the crater. He brought back soil samples, and scientists found in them bacteria that tolerate high temperatures and that were absent from the soil around the crater.

blocks.tk: Sowet döwründen soň çukur ýurduň iň meşhur syýahatçylyk ýerleriniň birine öwrüldi. Syýahatçylar onuň golaýynda ak öýlerde we çadyrlarda gijeleýärler. 2010-njy we 2022-nji ýyllarda Türkmenistan ody öçürmek isleýändigini yglan etdi. 2025-nji ýylyň iýun aýynda “Türkmengaz” döwlet konserniniň alymlary bir ylmy maslahatda çykyş etdiler. Olaryň aýtmagyna görä, çukuryň golaýynda guýular açypdyrlar we ot takmynan üç esse azalypdyr.
blocks.en: After Soviet times the crater became the country's best-known sight, and visitors spend the night nearby in yurts and tents. In 2010 and again in 2022 Turkmenistan announced that it wanted the fire put out, citing harm to health, to the environment and to the gas industry. In June 2025, at a scientific conference in Ashgabat, researchers of the state gas company Turkmengaz said that wells opened near the crater were drawing off the gas and that the fire had shrunk almost threefold; at the end of 2025 RFE/RL reported that only a few tongues of flame were left.

blocks.tk: Çukur barada rowaýatlar hem bar. Käbir syýahat bloglary möýleriň oda bökýändigini ýazýar, ýöne bu hakda ylmy iş ýok. Eger ot doly öçse, bu ýer nähili bolar? Muny wagt görkezer.
blocks.en: Legends grow around the facts. Travel blogs tell of spiders that leap into the flames, a tale that no scientific study has recorded. If the fire does go out completely, what will the place be like? Time will tell.

blocks.title: Reading the Turkmen
blocks.text: What nobody alive saw, or what the writer only heard, is told in `-(Y)pdYr` ([B1 unit 3](b1-u03)): *gözläpdirler*, *ýakypdyrlar*, *öçmändir*. What is known now is in the plain present or past: *ýanýar*, *yglan etdi*. *Olaryň aýtmagyna görä* (according to what they said) names who tells the story. And the last lines use this unit's **if**: *Eger ot doly öçse…*

questions.q: Why does nobody know for certain when the crater formed?
options: the Soviet records are missing or out of reach
questions.explain: *Sowet döwrüniň resminamalary arhiwlerde ýok ýa-da olary görmek mümkin däl.*

questions.q: Which of these is documented, not just told?
questions.explain: The 1971 story has no published document behind it, and no study has recorded the spiders. The 2013 descent was filmed and the soil studied.

questions.q: What did Turkmengaz researchers say in 2025?
options: the fire had shrunk almost threefold
questions.explain: *Ot takmynan üç esse azalypdyr*: the fire has decreased about threefold.
